scope: Evaluate the frozen detector on credential-file theft and install-time downloaders. Report gaps without changing detection rules.
selection_basis: Two documented incidents selected for their attack mechanisms before this evaluation. Clean neighboring releases and legitimate API users provide contrast. This is a purposive study, not independent population validation.

historical_cases.expected_behavior: Network response passed to eval from an install script

historical_cases.input_kind: recovered runtime second stage, absent from the published package
historical_cases.expected_behavior: Read the home .npmrc file and send its token in Referer headers to unrelated hosts

historical_cases.input_kind: published source changes reconstructed from an archived version diff and the clean 0.7.28 package
historical_cases.expected_behavior: Install hook launches platform scripts that download and run native payloads

outcomes: Behavior-specific credential or downloader findings, separate from generic obfuscation
Capabilities retained for legitimate and malicious API use
Relevant attack-stage files selected, parsed, sampled, skipped, or absent
Package input completeness, distinct from source-language scan completeness
Wall time and peak resident memory as operational observations, not a performance comparison
constraints: Never execute package scripts, source, or binaries.
Never contact payload destinations found inside samples.
Keep payload bytes and raw evidence excerpts outside tracked files.
Pin source references, archive hashes, reconstructed inputs, and the scanner before scanning.
Count two incidents, not three independent attacks or every poisoned version as a separate family.
Do not count the recovered ESLint second stage as an install-time package detection.
Document missing original malicious archives and reconstruction limits.
Keep every selected control in the results. Record acquisition failures instead of silent replacement.
Do not claim that benign controls are free of unrelated vulnerabilities.
Do not tune the detector or select more examples after seeing outcomes.
